name: reading-instrument/p3-module-graphite
refs: MATERIALS (a reference the owner chose): take ONLY the moulded plastic: separate housing panels with real bevelled edges, seams between them, small screws, recessed modules. Do not take its pixel style, its colours, its screens or its density.

THE CURRENT HOUSING (project-owned, the owner likes it): match its plastic exactly: the same warm dark graphite, the same satin bevels, the same cross-head screws, the same black rubber bezel and the same dark teal glass with its window reflection.
prompt:
Paint, flat-on and centred, ONE small moulded plastic MODULE of a home research instrument for a cosy creature-breeding game, a finished painted game asset: a square module with a THICK rounded moulded frame (about 7 percent of the width on every side, a little deeper at the bottom), its outer edge softly rounded with a real bevel catching a soft top light, a fine parting seam running round the frame, a small cross-head screw in each of its four corners, then a matte black RUBBER GASKET (about 1.5 percent, soft, no shine) holding the GLASS. The glass is dark, EMPTY and deep: a deep blue-green teal going near-black at its corners, a very faint even light from inside, a soft broad diagonal reflection across its upper left, a thin specular line along its top inner edge; nothing drawn on the glass. The module is MOUNTED in a darker CHASSIS PLATE that shows as an even margin all round it (about 5 percent of the width on every side): the plate is a darker matte graphite with a fine moulded texture, and the module sits slightly raised on it, with a soft contact shadow under its bottom edge and a thin dark gap between module and plate. The plate's margin is plain (no screws, no features) and even on all four sides so it can be stretched. Light: soft and real, a top light from a warm room. No neon, no light lines, no bloom. The module's plastic is the same warm dark GRAPHITE grey as the reference housing, matte with a slight satin sheen on the bevels; the rubber is black.
NO text, letters, digits, logos or icons anywhere. The chassis plate fills the canvas edge to edge: no table, no wall, no background.
